name: Proto-Southern Vanuatu
notes: Reconstructed by Lynch (2001) from Proto Erromango, Proto Tanna and Anejom, with its development from POc. Lynch (2001: 13, 184) groups the Southern Vanuatu languages as Erromango (Sye, Ura, Utaha), Tanna (Northern: North Tanna, Whitesands, Lenakel; Southern: Southwest Tanna, Kwamera) and Anejom. Lynch places Southern Vanuatu in Southern Oceanic (pp. 6, 190) but enters no PSOc changes of his own; the Southern Oceanic group (soc) is a linkage here (decision pocr-parents). Changes in canonical form that are not segment correspondences are in the notes only: loss of pretonic vowels (*na lima-ña > Lenakel nelman), accretion of an initial vowel to most verbs and of the article *na to most nouns, and retention of POc final consonants, which the Erromangan languages tend to lose after nasals and Anejom loses except *r (p. 14; Table 4.1, p. 102). Glottocode sout2868 (Southern Vanuatu), same membership.

name: Proto-Erromango
notes: Lynch (2001: 13-91). Utaha (Ifo) data are 'highly tentative, based as they are on the most fragmentary of data' and are given only in the tables of correspondences (p. 13). Lynch also reconstructs medial clusters *n + *r (Sye nr, Ura d-, -d-, -n; p. 42) and *n + *t (Sye nt, Ura d; pp. 53, 55), from the accreted article and from compounds; these are not entered as phonemes. Glottocode erro1239 (Erromanga), same membership.

name: Proto-Tanna
notes: Lynch (2001: 13-99). Two subgroups, Northern and Southern Tanna (p. 13; justified in ch. 8). POc *l, *r and *R merged as PTn *r (p. 45). Glottocode tann1242 (Tanna), same membership.

name: Proto-Northern Tanna
notes: Given by Lynch (2001) only in Appendix I (pp. 201-203) and in the discussion of the liquids and sibilants (pp. 45-47, 66): PTn *r split into PNT *l and *i, and PTn *h into *h and *z. Glottocode nort3218 (Northern Tanna linkage in Glottolog), same membership.

name: Proto-Southern Tanna
notes: Given by Lynch (2001) only in Appendix I (pp. 201-203), where every PST phoneme is the same as in PTn (*q is marked '?'). Glottocode sout3195 (Southern Tanna), same membership.

name: Ura
notes: Erromango; moribund (Lynch 2001: 4-5). Lynch (2001: 7) quotes Terry Crowley on the considerable variation between [l] and [r] in Ura transcriptions. Many Ura words with medial t are probably Sye loans (Lynch 2001: 55). Coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023: 629).

name: Utaha
notes: Extinct language of Erromango. Lynch's Utaha reflexes are 'highly tentative, based as they are on the most fragmentary of data' (2001: 13), and the vowels could not be worked out (p. 91). Glottolog name Ifo.

name: North Tanna
notes: The dialect Lynch cites has, besides the voiceless stops, an incomplete set of prenasalised voiced stops /ᵐbʷ ᵐb ⁿd/; other dialects have the Lenakel system (2001: 7). It is not clear whether North Tanna and Whitesands have /w/ (p. 7, n. 6); not entered. Coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023: 627).

name: Whitesands
notes: Same consonant system as Lenakel, perhaps also with /fʷ/ (Lynch 2001: 7); whether it has /w/ is not clear (p. 7, n. 6), and /w/ is not entered. Coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023: 629).

name: Lenakel
notes: Lynch's own field language (2001: 7). Vowel length is contrastive, mostly in final syllables (p. 8); not entered. Coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023: 625).

name: Southwest Tanna
notes: Same system as Kwamera, except that most dialects have /l/ for /r/ (Lynch 2001: 7-8); the Mess dialect has r (p. 45, n. 15). Coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023: 628).

name: Kwamera
notes: Kwamera fluctuates between s and h more than the other Tanna languages (Lynch 2001: 65). Vowel length is contrastive (p. 8); not entered. Coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023: 625).
